subject: physics
question_text: Define the angle of friction and the angle of repose. Show that they are equal.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The two definitions
lines: Angle of friction φ: the angle between the
normal force and the resultant of the normal
Angle of repose θ: the angle of an incline at
which a body on it just begins to slide.
steps.why: One is measured on a flat surface, the other on a slope — which is exactly why it is worth proving they are the same number.
common_mistakes: Defining the angle of friction as the angle between the friction force and the surface.
Defining φ as the angle between the normal force and the limiting friction — that angle is always 90°. φ is between the normal and the RESULTANT of the normal force and the limiting friction.

recall.must_convey: That the angle of friction is between the normal force and the resultant, and the angle of repose is the incline angle at which the body just slides.
accept: between the normal and the resultant
incline angle at which it just slides

steps.label: The two relations
lines: At the angle of friction, the resultant is
made of f_s across and N along, so
At the angle of repose the body just slides,
so weight down the slope = limiting friction:

lines.text: m g sin θ = μ_s m g cos θ

steps.why: The mg cancels in the second line, which is why the angle of repose depends on the surfaces alone and never on the body. Here f_s is the limiting (maximum) static friction. Below the limit friction is smaller than μ_s N, and the resultant then makes an angle smaller than φ with the normal.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the normal force on an incline is mg cos θ, not mg.

recall.must_convey: That tan phi equals mu s from the resultant, and mg sin theta equals mu s mg cos theta gives tan theta equals mu s.
accept: tan phi equals f by N equals mu
mg sin theta equals mu mg cos theta
reject: between the normal and the resultant

steps.label: The result
lines: Both tangents equal the same μ_s, so

lines.text: tan φ = tan θ   ∴   φ = θ

lines: The angle of repose IS the angle of friction,
measured on a slope instead of a flat table.
steps.why: Two different experiments give the same number because both are really measuring one thing: the ratio f/N for that pair of surfaces.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the two tangents without stating that the angles themselves are equal.

recall.must_convey: That both tangents equal mu s, so phi equals theta.
reject: mg sin theta equals mu mg cos theta
